analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/cache-aware-routing.md (head text shown, no diff) and docs/architecture/inference.md (patch). No code, auth, attestation, encryption, billing or dispatch logic changes in the visible input, so I found no concrete regression.

Things the next pass should check against the real code, which was not supplied:
- inference.md ~L261-267 says the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_KV_QUANTIZATION key is accepted by DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification and the serving-profile check, only for native precision. If the code allows non-native values, that would loosen the environment guard that protects deadline qualification and serving-profile admission. The guard's code paths are not in this input.
- inference.md ~L666-690 describes balanced checkpoint storage, lossy older-row reconstruction, and live-packed slots using a 'complete packed checkpoint contract'. This touches the SSD prefix-cache artifact format under T-041 (leak #2 closed by HMAC names, AES-GCM, DBK3 AAD, 30-minute TTL). I could not confirm that packed or compressed checkpoints keep nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookup tag in the metadata or AAD, or that they keep the same salt scoping, TTL and KEK purge. The T-041 detection_hint on DBK3 metadata and AAD applies.
- cache-aware-routing.md contains the attempt-byte budget, persistence/restore, fence and status sections. They describe an aggregate-only /v1/cache/status that exposes no account, scope or provider labels, and keyed identifiers only in the durable copy. These agree with T-003/T-041 and Invariant 7 as written. I cannot confirm the code matches (cachetracker, cachepersist), because that code is outside this batch.

No threat-model definition is invalidated by the prose. Coverage limit: the Go and Swift sources the docs cite were not provided.
